chunks: He is exalted above what those who define (limit) attribute to Him, from the qualities of measures and extremities, and the inhabiting of dwellings and dwelling in places.
So the limit is struck for His creation, and is attributed to other than Him.

key_terms.الْمُحَدِّدُونَ: Those who define or limit (God), attributing spatial boundaries to Him
key_terms.تَمَكُّنِ الْأَمَاكِنِ: Dwelling in or being confined to places

ai.seo_question: How does Shia theology describe God's transcendence from physical space and limits?
ai.summary: Sharif al-Radi presents this passage as a cornerstone of Shia theological discourse on *Tanzih* (divine transcendence), explicitly rejecting anthropomorphic attributes (*tashbih*) by distinguishing between the Creator's essence and created spatial limitations. The text emphasizes that while boundaries and locations are imposed upon creation, God is free from such constraints, a concept deeply rooted in the Mu'tazili-influenced rational theology favored by the Ahl al-Bayt tradition.

en.sayed-ali-raza: He is far above what those whose regard is limited attribute to Him, such as the qualities of measure, having extremities, living in houses and dwelling in abodes,
because limits are meant for creation and are attributable only to other than Allāh.
